title: Duke's real talent: hearing riffs and writing to fit each man
summary: Bigard says Duke's talent was creative ideas and studying each player so his writing fit like a glove, turning solo riffs into new tunes, unlike Calloway, and Tyree Glenn says he listened to new men for two months.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: What do you think Duke's biggest talent was? Composition or managing people or playing or what?

I think -- No -- I think -- not playing, not by a longshot. His talents, I mean, he was a creative man to begin with and he had marvelous ideas and which I give him a lot of credit because if he heard something, like I said, if I was playing a solo or something -- you know, like a little jazz thing of my own -- and he heard something he liked and he'd tell me, 'Play.' He wouldn't say, 'Play it again.' He just say, 'Keep on playing. Play.' And if I happened to make that thing again and the first thing you know in about three

or four days he's written a new tune from my riff that I put on, see, and he'd get away with things like that. So that was pretty smart, you know, because nobody else did ever do things like that. You take, like, -- Calloway had wonderful musicians in his band but he didn't know what to do with them, you see. And that's the comparison between leaders.

But Duke studied all his men. He studied what their style, how they maneuver with their music, with their playing and everything and he keeps that in his mind so if he wrote anything for you, it fit you like a glove, you know, and you're really at home while you're playing it. It's not something that he just was taking it from his head and making it, trying to see how difficult he could make it or anything. No, it wasn't like that.

Tyree Glenn said once that Duke would listen to each new man that he'd hire and listen to them for maybe two months in the band before he would write for them or sometimes before he would even give them any solos --
-- because he wanted to know what they sounded like, what their capabilities were, and how they would fit in the total scheme of things. Is that the way -- ?
